display.purpose: Application title in the 54px command bar.

components.name: Default Command Button
components.description: Compact file, edit, and cue commands in the command bar and Cue Book.
components.css: .ds-btn-default { background: #202b33; color: #f7f2e8; border: 1px solid #344550; border-radius: 4px; padding: 7px 10px; transition: background 0.15s, border-color 0.15s; } .ds-btn-default:hover { background: #293844; border-color: #496fc8; } .ds-btn-default:focus-visible { background: #26375b; border-color: #f0c96b; outline: none; }

components.name: Export PNG Button
components.description: Primary export action aligned to the command bar's right edge.
components.css: .ds-btn-export { background: #f0c96b; color: #1b2429; border: 1px solid #d3a34f; border-radius: 4px; padding: 7px 10px; transition: background 0.15s; } .ds-btn-export:hover { background: #f5dc9d; } .ds-btn-export:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #f7f2e8; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Cast Search Field
components.description: Filters Cast & Props by asset name or group.
components.css: .ds-input-search { background: #111827; color: #f7f2e8; border: 1px solid #344550; border-radius: 4px; padding: 7px 10px; } .ds-input-search::placeholder { color: #a8b1b4; } .ds-input-search:focus-visible { border-color: #f0c96b; outline: none; }

components.name: Cast Asset Tile
components.description: Two-column 120×58 selectable asset tile showing name and footprint.
components.css: .ds-asset-tile { width: 120px; height: 58px; background: #202b33; color: #f7f2e8; border: 1px solid #344550; border-radius: 4px; padding: 7px 10px; text-align: left; } .ds-asset-tile:hover { border-color: #496fc8; } .ds-asset-tile:focus-visible { background: #26375b; border-color: #f0c96b; outline: none; } .ds-asset-tile small { color: #a8b1b4; }

components.name: Cue Book Panel
components.description: Compact right-side inspector for selected piece, layer actions, and grid cue.
components.css: .ds-cue-book { background: #182128; color: #f7f2e8; border-left: 1px solid #344550; padding: 10px 12px; } .ds-cue-book h2 { color: #f7f2e8; font-size: 17px; font-weight: 400; } .ds-cue-book p { color: #a8b1b4; font-size: 12px; }

components.name: Stage Canvas
components.description: Dominant 24×16 map stage with optional square/hex grid and pixel-piece selection.
components.css: .ds-stage { min-width: 720px; min-height: 480px; background: #263d2c; border: 1px solid #344550; position: relative; overflow: hidden; } .ds-stage:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #f0c96b; outline-offset: -2px; }

narrative.overview:
This is a stage-first desktop tool: the painted map owns the center, while editor chrome is deliberately dark, quiet, and cue-like. The permanent left Cast & Props rail and compact right Cue Book frame a wide central stage. Cobalt marks active states, cue gold marks the primary action and section cues, dusty rose is reserved for removal/warning language, and warm paper text keeps the dark shell legible.

The implemented surface uses Godot's default sans-serif at a compact desktop scale. Panels are flat tonal blocks joined by one-pixel seams; controls use small 4px corners and restrained internal padding. The canvas supports a painted/placeholder landscape, square or hex grid overlays, and crisp pixel-style pieces with a warm selection keyline.
keyCharacteristics: Stage-black shell with panel tonal layering and hairline seams.
Permanent 276px Cast & Props library, dominant center stage, 260px Cue Book.
Cobalt active controls; cue-gold Export PNG and section headings.
Crisp pixel-art silhouettes over painted/placeholder terrain; no shadows in the UI chrome.

rules.name: The Cue-Gold Rule
rules.body: Reserve gold for primary action, cue headings, and selection feedback so it reads as a stage direction rather than decoration.

rules.name: The Flat Stagecraft Rule
rules.body: Use tonal layering and hairline seams for editor structure; do not add generic card shadows to the shell.

dos: Do keep the map visually dominant between the fixed 276px and 260px rails.
Do preserve crisp pixel silhouettes over atmospheric/painted terrain.
Do use cobalt for active state, cue gold for primary cues, and dusty rose for removal/warnings.
Do keep labels clear and pair pointer actions with the implemented keyboard shortcuts (Ctrl+S/O/Z/Y/D, R, Delete).
donts: Don't introduce manual piece resizing; footprints are asset-defined and snap to whole cells.
Don't turn the editor into an encounter tracker; encounter statistics are out of scope.
Don't replace the flat, seam-led shell with generic shadow-heavy cards.
Don't let chrome compete with the stage or soften pixel-art edges with filtering.
